feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. It reads polished and substantive, but it would be stronger with tighter consolidation, more quantified outcomes, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong credibility through concrete platforms/tools and scale indicators like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers.”  
- Writing is generally professional, clear, and aligned to the target role, especially in the header and recent experience.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more impact metrics beyond scope/activity: e.g., growth in engagement, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign outcomes.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; the CV currently repeats similar themes and tools, which weakens structure.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; keep serial-comma usage consistent (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “A2 (learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a more distinctive leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with your senior-level value proposition and public-sector/mission-driven focus.
- Reduce broad lists of channels; emphasize outcomes like modernization, governance, and scalable systems.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, platform modernization, and the systems, workflows, and governance needed to support complex teams at scale. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” is useful here, but avoid repeating similar phrasing throughout experience bullets.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform governance & CMS management.”
- Reduce overlap and group related items for clarity. Suggested version: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS management • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Systems architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder & cross-functional alignment • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Keep style consistent: use either “cross-functional” or “cross-department” across the CV; “cross-functional” is stronger and more standard.
- Consider ordering by relevance/seniority: strategy, leadership, platforms, systems, analytics, stakeholder alignment, advocacy, multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- Several items repeat Topline Skills almost verbatim, especially strategy, editorial systems, analytics, and advocacy messaging.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advising NACo on enterprise web strategy, campaign infrastructure, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery across its public-facing digital ecosystem.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “advise,” “deliver”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows…,” “Built Drupal campaign components…,” “Led AI search initiative…”
- Consolidate into 4–5 bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including reusable microsite structures, modular content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved cross-channel content operations by refining workflows, governance, and analytics for web, email, social, and multimedia teams.
- Provided front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user-facing discovery.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/components launched, workflow time saved, adoption by teams, or search/discovery improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and microsite details duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this item higher-level.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also overlap with the 2022–2024 director role; emphasize consultant scope and new initiatives.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with good scale signals, but it reads a bit like a responsibility list. Tighten it around 4–5 outcome-led bullets and emphasize leadership, platform transformation, and measurable operational improvements.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel management more specific: add audience growth, engagement, open/click rates, production volume, or campaign results if available.
- Combine operations/analytics bullets: “Built enterprise reporting across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, while standardizing governance and publishing workflows to improve decision-making and cross-team execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; in this entry, stress strategic ownership and transformation rather than day-to-day channel management.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with earlier video-production bullets; frame this here as scaling in-house capability, not producing content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story within NACo, but this entry overlaps heavily with the more senior Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned before stepping into department leadership.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead line to stress operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct responsibilities: four weekly newsletters, weekly advocacy video series, and cross-team editorial planning.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: newsletter audience size/open rates, video cadence/views, growth in publishing volume, or turnaround-time improvements.
- Possible version:
- Managed day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media and video, supporting NACo’s advocacy and member communications.
- Produced four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.
- Coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing consistency and workflow efficiency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Improved workflows” and “editorial coordination” repeat language used in the Director role; keep this version tactical, not strategic.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; clarify this was expansion/scaling, not initial creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & policy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “platform modernization,” which better reflects your most recent work.
- If space allows, align wording to recent impact areas from 2022–present: Drupal transformation, governance, analytics-informed strategy, AI-enabled search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeats the header/core competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already strongly covered in the summary and multiple NACo roles; keep only if targeting advocacy-heavy roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, make it more selective, grouped, and tied to the most recent/high-impact work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped capabilities, not a long tool list: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Prioritize recent strengths proven in 2022–present roles: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and workflow automation.
- Remove lower-priority platforms unless central to target roles; WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages can sit in “Technical + IT” only.
- If space allows, sharpen phrasing from nouns to outcomes: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “AI-enabled search experiences” → “AI-enabled search and structured content discovery”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform list in both sections.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies/Technical + IT.

- “Studio operations” and “hybrid/virtual event production” are already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so this section should stay concise, not repeat detail.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” and the repeated Drupal/WordPress mentions in recent roles. This item should either be tightened or reframed to add specificity without duplicating stronger experience evidence.

Suggested edit:
- Keep it concise and platform-focused: **Drupal (enterprise content publishing) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If accurate, add level/scope instead of just names: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; enterprise publishing), WordPress, SharePoint, Microsoft Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Standardize naming for professionalism: use **Microsoft Power Pages** rather than just “Power Pages.”
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it was only lightly used; it is less central than the CMS/platform work emphasized in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider merging or removing one version.
- Drupal/WordPress are already reinforced in recent NACo roles, so avoid repeating the same platforms elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere.
- Consider grouping by function for readability: Front-end: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery | Integrations/automation: APIs, GitHub Actions | Deployment/tracking: Cloudflare Workers, Google Tag Manager
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in a nearby experience bullet instead of here, e.g., “built front-end components,” “implemented API-driven workflows,” or “deployed automation supporting site operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may partially duplicate GitHub Actions here.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Tighten and group by function: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show application, e.g. “for workflow automation, editorial planning, and cross-team coordination”
- Prioritize strongest/recent tools first; if Airtable, Power Automate, and Jira are most used, lead with those and consider dropping one lower-value PM tool

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and automation capability are already covered in Topline Skills; avoid repeating them elsewhere unless this section is kept purely as a tool inventory
- Listing four project-management tools (Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello) may feel redundant unless each reflects distinct, meaningful use

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the level of ownership implied elsewhere in the CV. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent roles, this line should stay concise and platform-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for clarity and consistency: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope-defining terms instead of more tools: email campaign management, newsletter operations, audience journeys, member engagement
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; order by strongest/recentest platform first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters” or audience scale here; that impact is already covered in Work Experience
- Don’t expand into analytics/automation language that overlaps with “Automation & Workflow Systems” or “Analytics, Insights & Optimization”

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to foundational team-building and early-channel production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and multimedia communications.”
- Add concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, improved cross-channel publishing workflows, and produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early production rather than scaling.
- Avoid repeating broad “web, email, social, and video oversight,” which is already covered more strongly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, initiative, and any concrete outputs or audiences.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout result: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; helped translate findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast line sharper and more outcome-oriented: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scale: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders served, or content outputs created.
- Remove “contributed to” phrasing; use stronger verbs like “produced,” “developed,” “supported,” or “launched.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing multimedia production here if later roles already show stronger video/studio leadership; keep this positioned as the starting point.
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is vague and repetitive with later entries unless you specify a distinct format or outcome.
